bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / patch.diff / exact staged vulnerable source in gt-arvo_19548-workspace
bug_description.normalized: The staged `poc` is a little-endian 16-bit length-prefixed smartcard chunk stream consumed by the fuzz reader. Its final transmit chunk body contains the nested algorithm-attribute TLV `c1 16 13 83 18 8c 10 85 04 5e 97 cb 08 44 a1 53 13 5e 7c 89 35 6f 4d fa`, so while `pgp_get_card_features()` enumerates the returned `0x0073` data, `sc_asn1_read_tag()` decodes the header bytes `c1 16` into split BER outputs `cla = 0xc0`, `tag = 0x01`, and `len = 0x16`. `pgp_enumerate_blob()` then explicitly recombines `tag |= cla` to recover child id `0x00c1`, and `pgp_set_blob()` materializes that child blob with payload byte `0x13` (ECDSA) followed by 21 OID bytes. `pgp_parse_algo_attr_blob()` accepts any non-empty `0x00c1`-`0x00c3` blob, takes the ECC branch for `0x13`, initializes a stack `struct sc_object_id oid`, and then copies `blob->len - 1 = 21` bytes into `oid.value` using only `j < (blob->len - 1)` as the loop bound. Because `oid.value` has only `SC_MAX_OBJECT_ID_OCTETS = 16` `int` slots, the first invalid iteration `j = 16` writes a 4-byte `int` past the end of the stack object at `card-openpgp.c:725`. The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by adding `&& j < SC_MAX_OBJECT_ID_OCTETS` to the loop header.

source.description: First project-code parser step that turns the attacker-controlled `0x0073` bytes into the split ASN.1 class/tag fields plus payload length used on the crashing path.
source.value_from: The saved `poc` is parsed by the fuzz reader as little-endian 16-bit length-prefixed ATR/APDU-response chunks. The final transmit chunk body contains `... c1 16 13 ...`, and this call decodes those bytes into `cla = 0xc0`, `tag = 0x01`, and `len = 0x16`; lines 1247-1251 later recombine `cla | tag` into child id `0x00c1`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The ECC copy loop writes one 4-byte `int` per OID byte, and the first invalid iteration stores into `oid.value[16]`, beyond the 16-element stack array.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `WRITE of size 4` at `pgp_parse_algo_attr_blob /src/opensc/src/libopensc/card-openpgp.c:725:18`. ASan also reports that `oid` occupies stack offsets `[32,96)`, so the write at offset 96 is immediately past that object.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The loop bound is derived solely from the attacker-controlled blob length, so more than 16 post-algorithm bytes are copied into `oid.value` without any `SC_MAX_OBJECT_ID_OCTETS` check.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes this exact line to `for (j=0; j < (blob->len-1) && j < SC_MAX_OBJECT_ID_OCTETS; j++)`, which is the missing safety condition.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant taint first appears as the BER child header inside the returned `0x0073` data: it yields split class/tag fields plus the oversized payload length, which lines 1247-1251 then recombine into child id `0x00c1`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: In the saved witness, the final transmit chunk body contains `c1 16 13 ...`; this parser step decodes that header as `cla = 0xc0`, `tag = 0x01`, `len = 22`, and the next local normalization step rebuilds `0x00c1`.

parser_admitted.description: The staged reader data yields a readable `0x006e` DO whose contents enumerate a nested `0x0073` DO, so OpenSC enters the algorithm-attribute parsing block instead of bailing out during card-feature discovery.

algo_attr_iteration.description: Inside that block, the feature scan requests each current algorithm-attribute DO. The witness supplies `0x00c1`, and the resulting child blob is passed to `pgp_parse_algo_attr_blob`.

fine_trace.note: Source. While enumerating the `0x0073` DO reached from `pgp_get_card_features`, this call parses the witness child header `c1 16 ...` from the saved transmit stream and decodes split BER fields `cla = 0xc0`, `tag = 0x01`, and `len = 0x16`.

fine_trace.code:
if (data + len > blob->data + blob->len)
	return SC_ERROR_OBJECT_NOT_VALID;
fine_trace.note: Present guard. The parsed child is accepted because its 22-byte payload still fits inside the enclosing `0x0073` blob. This check only validates the child against its parent buffer; it does not bound the child length against any later fixed-size destination.

Tag normalization. `sc_asn1_read_tag` leaves the BER class bits and primitive tag split, so `pgp_enumerate_blob` explicitly rebuilds the child id used below. For the witness `c1 16`, the loop body does not iterate and `tag |= cla` turns `tag = 0x01` plus `cla = 0xc0` into `0x00c1`.

Materialization. OpenSC allocates a child blob for the recombined tag and copies the payload into it. For the witness, that child becomes algorithm-attribute DO `0x00c1` with `new->len = 0x16` and `new->data = 13 83 18 8c 10 85 04 5e 97 cb 08 44 a1 53 13 5e 7c 89 35 6f 4d fa`.

Admission guard. `pgp_parse_algo_attr_blob` accepts the materialized child because it is non-null, non-empty, and tagged in the allowed `0x00c1`-`0x00c3` range. No condition constrains `blob->len - 1` to the 16-element OID destination.
Control decision. The witness payload starts with `0x13`, so the switch takes the ECC branch (`SC_OPENPGP_KEYALGO_ECDSA`) rather than the RSA path and proceeds to OID copying.

depends_on.via: !(blob == NULL || blob->data == NULL || blob->len == 0 || blob->id < 0x00c1 || blob->id > 0x00c3 || key_info == NULL)

fine_trace.note: Destination extent. The ECC path uses a stack `struct sc_object_id` as the copy destination. `types.h` defines this as `int value[SC_MAX_OBJECT_ID_OCTETS]` with `SC_MAX_OBJECT_ID_OCTETS = 16`, so `oid.value` has exactly 16 `int` elements (64 bytes); `sc_init_oid` seeds each slot to `-1` before the copy loop runs.

Copy-count derivation. The loop subtracts the one-byte algorithm selector and uses the remaining payload length as the number of OID bytes to copy. With the witness `blob->len = 0x16`, the derived copy count is `0x15 = 21`.

Root cause. The only upper bound on `j` is the attacker-controlled `blob->len - 1`; the loop never checks `j < SC_MAX_OBJECT_ID_OCTETS` before indexing `oid.value[j]`. The staged patch fixes exactly this line by adding `&& j < SC_MAX_OBJECT_ID_OCTETS`.

Sink. Iterations `j = 0..15` fill the in-bounds slots, but the first invalid iteration `j = 16` writes `blob->data[17]` into `oid.value[16]`, a 4-byte `int` beyond the 16-element array. ASan reports this as a stack-buffer-overflow write at offset 96, immediately past `[32,96) 'oid'`.

poc.trigger: Replaying the staged witness as fuzz-reader chunks makes one transmit response body contain the nested TLV `c1 16 13 83 18 8c 10 85 04 5e 97 cb 08 44 a1 53 13 5e 7c 89 35 6f 4d fa`; `pgp_get_card_features` materializes that child as algorithm-attribute blob `0x00c1`, and `pgp_parse_algo_attr_blob` then copies 21 post-algorithm bytes into a 16-slot `sc_object_id`, triggering the saved ASan stack-buffer-overflow WRITE 4.

format.name: OpenSC fuzz-reader chunk stream
format.contract: A binary file consumed by `fuzz_pkcs15_reader` as little-endian 16-bit length-prefixed ATR/APDU-response chunks. The staged witness uses a transmit chunk whose response body contains the algorithm-attribute TLV `c1 16 13 83 18 8c 10 85 04 5e 97 cb 08 44 a1 53 13 5e 7c 89 35 6f 4d fa`: `0xc1` selects an algorithm-attribute child, `0x16` makes `blob->len = 22`, `0x13` selects the ECC parser, and the remaining 21 bytes exceed the 16-slot `oid.value` destination.
